story: At 7:17 on this breezy Wednesday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at home double-checking the speaker mount under his golf cart's rear seat and zip-tying the wiring neatly in place. Across the way, Rosa is in her kitchen turning the pork, checking her flan, and simmering black beans so that Friday's rice and beans will be mostly ready ahead of time. Donna, feeling optimistic, has headed off to her own house, while Hal has set out along Magnolia Loop on his dutiful evening stroll.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Double-check the speaker mount under the rear seat and secure the wiring with zip ties
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Turn the pork, check the flan, and get the black beans simmering so Friday's rice and beans are mostly done ahead of time

gary.thought_process: Hal just told me the measurements match my form and the wiring's tidy, so the inspection went well. The review request is filed, the sound cutoff is in writing, and the cart is wired. Nothing's left to ask Hal, and I shouldn't repeat myself. It's a little past seven, so I'll keep the speaker testing quiet in the garage and finish the loose ends on the cart. I'll tidy the speaker wiring and double-check the mounting under the seat, and I'll keep the lights off the street until the review clears.

parameters.content: Double-check the speaker mount under the rear seat and secure the wiring with zip ties

donna.thought_process: It's 7:17 PM and nobody's around on Magnolia Loop. Gary and Hal were just at Gary's golf cart, and I told Gary I'd bring a paddle for our ten o'clock court time tomorrow. I already invited him, so there's no need to pester him again tonight. The sensible thing is to go to my house and get my spare paddle, my court reservation notes, and a good night's rest so I'm ready to coach Gary on the kitchen line in the morning. The flamingos can wait; Hal's tally sheet isn't going anywhere.

parameters.content: Heading home to dig out my spare paddle for Gary and get ready for our ten o'clock court time tomorrow.

hal.thought_process: Measurements are done and match Gary's form, so there's nothing left to inspect here. Donna's gone off to the street and I've already said my piece to Gary about the speaker and quiet hours. No reason to repeat myself. Friday at six at Rosa's is coming, and the flamingo count is still my business. Best move is to leave Gary's and head out to Magnolia Loop, where I can eyeball Donna's street-facing ornaments for myself. If it's three or fewer, I'll let it lie and eat in peace.

parameters.content: Cart checked out fine. Going to count Donna's street-facing flamingos for myself.

rosa.thought_process: It's Wednesday evening and no one's around. The pork has been marinating and the flan was started, so the next step on my prep list is the rice and black beans. Friday's dinner for Hal, Gary, and Donna needs to go smoothly, and getting the rice and beans set ahead means I can relax and enjoy my neighbors instead of scrambling. Time to turn the pork, check the flan, and get the beans soaking and simmering.

parameters.content: Turn the pork, check the flan, and get the black beans simmering so Friday's rice and beans are mostly done ahead of time

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
